correctness.rationale: Exact orbit averaging applies globally. The explicit zero-sum Rayleigh vector has squared norm n(3n^3+5n^2-8n+4). An exact convex combination of its quotient and the right-leaf eigenvalue equals a positive combination of the two hub capacity constraints. This proves lambda_2<=b*. At the candidate, the 4-orbit polynomial factors as x(x-b*)q_n(x); the four exact sign/derivative inequalities enclose both real q roots between b* and 2-b*. The remaining leaf eigenvalues are in that interval. Thus the infinite theorem follows without extrapolation from finite tests.

value.rationale: An asymmetric tree with multiple leaf orbits is a natural stress test of mixing design: separate stochastic hub capacities and repeated leaf eigenvalues compete. The theorem gives an exact infinite-family rational optimum, explicit optimal positive edge weights, and a short sharp dual certificate for why the bottleneck is active. It solves a meaningful optimization rather than a renamed numerical case.
